subject: general
question: Why is legal enforceability of rules important in a society?

options.text: It provides assurance that others will follow the rules.
It gives power to the police only.
So people can break them without fear

solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides assurance that others will follow the rules.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Legal enforceability ensures that individuals adhere to societal rules and regulations, fostering a harmonious and orderly environment.
 
• It creates a system of accountability, deterring people from violating laws due to potential penalties.
 
• A legally enforced framework maintains fairness and equality by applying rules uniformly to all members of society.
 
• It provides a sense of security, as individuals trust that disputes or violations will be resolved through an impartial legal process.
 
• By ensuring compliance, legal enforceability aids in preventing anarchy and upholding social order and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal enforceability:** Refers to the formal application of laws by authorities to ensure compliance and address violations.
 
• **Rule of law:** A principle under which all individuals, institutions, and entities are accountable to laws that are fairly applied and enforced.
 
• **Justice system:** Plays a crucial role in enforcing legal rules, resolving disputes, and penalizing unlawful actions to maintain social harmony.
 
• **Social contract theory:** Suggests that individuals consent to follow rules and laws in exchange for protection and benefits provided by the society and state.
 
• **Consequences of lawlessness:** Lack of legal enforceability can lead to chaos, increased crime rates, and the breakdown of societal structures.
